answer: Each agent can earn influence only by locking a scarce, nontransferable deposit for a fixed period, then gaining a capped share of rewards through verified work accepted by randomly assigned peers. A juniper node may submit claims, but a new vertex identity must lock its own ferrous collateral; splitting into sybils therefore multiplies the capital tied up and the time before it can be recovered. Provably false claims slash the deposit, making fake identities costly without assuming names are unique.
